name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The moderator needs to be able to create, manage, and guide estimation sessions to help the team collectively set sprint goals.
The moderator needs to be able to manage the estimation process, including accepting estimates and re-estimating, to ensure the team reaches consensus.
The moderator needs efficient ways to set up games, add stories, and manage participants to minimize administrative overhead.
The moderator needs to be able to access and export past game data for review and analysis.
The moderator needs to be able to create, log in, and manage their user account securely.
The moderator needs to be able to configure game settings such as estimation scales and participant limits to suit team preferences.
The estimator needs to be able to join games and submit their estimates for stories.
The estimator needs to be able to view the current story and all stories for the session to make informed estimates.
The participant needs to be able to see other participants' estimates and track the estimation process to facilitate discussion.
The participant needs to be able to manage a countdown timer to help regulate discussion length.
The participant needs a consistent interface and the ability to personalize their presence in the game.
The developer needs to build the application to comply with web standards and function across various browsers and accessibility guidelines.
The developer needs to implement technical solutions like database indexing to ensure the application is fast and stable.
The developer needs to design the application with sensible URLs and helpful error pages to enhance user experience.
The researcher needs access to game data stored in a non-identifiable format to conduct studies on estimation patterns.
lowLevelGoals: The moderator can initiate a new Planning Poker session by sending a request to the server.
The moderator can add a new user story to the current estimation session by providing story details via an API call.
The moderator can move the estimation session to the next story in the queue by triggering an API endpoint.
The moderator can trigger the display of all submitted estimates for the current story to all participants via an API call.
The moderator can mark a specific estimate as the final agreed-upon estimate for the current story by sending an API request.
The moderator can clear all submitted estimates for the current story, allowing for re-estimation, via an API call.
The moderator can generate and share a unique session invitation link or code via an API call.
The moderator can remove a specific participant from the current session by sending their ID to an API endpoint.
The moderator can terminate the active estimation session, archiving its data, via an API call.
The moderator can request a list of all previously conducted estimation sessions from the server via an API.
The moderator can download the data for a specific past session in a structured format (e.g., JSON, CSV) via an API endpoint.
The moderator can create a new user account by submitting registration details (e.g., email, password) to an API endpoint.
The moderator can authenticate their identity by sending login credentials to an API endpoint.
The moderator can modify their personal details (e.g., name, password) by sending an update request to an API endpoint.
The moderator can define or select different estimation scales (e.g., Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes) for a session via an API call.
The moderator can specify the maximum number of participants allowed in a session by sending a configuration update via an API.
The estimator can join a game by providing a valid session ID or invitation code to an API endpoint.
The estimator can send their chosen estimate value for the active story to the server via an API call.
The estimator can request and receive the description and context of the story currently being estimated via an API.
The estimator can request and receive a list of all stories planned for the current estimation session via an API.
The participant's client can subscribe to a WebSocket or long-polling API to receive immediate updates on other participants' estimates.
The participant can query an API to get the current status of the game (e.g., 'waiting for estimates', 'estimates revealed').
The participant can initiate a countdown timer for discussion by sending a request to an API endpoint.
The participant can temporarily halt the active countdown timer via an API call.
The participant can reset the countdown timer to its initial duration via an API call.
The participant can update their displayed name within the game session by sending a request to an API endpoint.
The participant can choose or upload an avatar to represent themselves in the game via an API call.
The developer will create and expose API endpoints for actions like creating sessions, adding stories, submitting estimates, and retrieving session data.
The developer will implement a WebSocket server to push real-time updates (e.g., estimate reveals, timer changes) to connected clients.
The developer will add indexes to database tables (e.g., sessions, stories, estimates) to speed up data retrieval operations.
The developer will integrate caching solutions (e.g., Redis, in-memory cache) for data that doesn't change often, reducing database load.
The developer will create clear and predictable URL paths for all accessible resources and API endpoints.
The developer will create dedicated error pages (e.g., 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error) to provide helpful feedback to users.
The developer will create an API endpoint that provides access to game data with all personally identifiable information removed or obfuscated.
The developer will ensure that any sensitive user data is anonymized or pseudonymized before being stored in the database for research purposes.
